section: Unemployment - types (structural, frictional, cyclical, disguised, seasonal, educated)
subsections: Cyclical unemployment - cause and business-cycle phase
Nature of India's unemployment - predominant type and causes

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the predominant sector and area associated with disguised unemployment?
o: Tourism and urban areas
Agriculture and rural areas
Financial services and rural areas
Manufacturing and urban areas
accepted.x: Disguised unemployment is predominantly found in agriculture, especially on family farms in rural areas.
accepted.tq: Use the sector-area pair rather than relying only on the name of the unemployment type.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Seasonal unemployment is common in agriculture, tourism and agro-industries.
2. Educated unemployment is predominantly an urban phenomenon.
3. Structural unemployment is generally short-term and temporary.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because structural unemployment is long-run in nature.
accepted.tq: Identify the duration trap in the statement describing structural unemployment.

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Type of unemployment)
A. Seasonal
B. Technological
C. Cyclical
D. Structural

List-II (Predominant area or condition)
1. Manufacturing and routine services
2. Industry and services during recession
3. Whole economy over the long run
4. Agriculture, tourism and agro-industries

Select the correct code:
accepted.x: Seasonal unemployment is associated with agriculture, tourism and agro-industries; technological unemployment with manufacturing and routine services; cyclical unemployment with recession-hit industry and services; and structural unemployment with the whole economy over the long run.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pairs and eliminate codes with a misplaced sector.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes rural and urban unemployment in India?
o: Educated unemployment is mainly rural, whereas disguised unemployment is mainly urban.
Seasonal and disguised unemployment are associated mainly with rural areas, whereas educated unemployment is mainly urban.
Structural unemployment is confined to agriculture, whereas technological unemployment is confined to tourism.
Cyclical unemployment occurs only in rural areas, whereas seasonal unemployment occurs only in cities.
accepted.x: NCERT identifies seasonal and disguised unemployment as major rural forms, while educated unemployment is predominantly urban.
accepted.tq: Compare the rural and urban pairs directly instead of matching one type with one area only.

accepted.s: With reference to open unemployment in Andhra Pradesh, which one of the following is correct according to the PLFS figures for 2023–24?
o: The rural rate was 5.9% and the urban rate was 3.4%.
The rural rate was 3.4% and the urban rate was 5.9%.
Both rural and urban rates were 3.4%.
Both rural and urban rates were 5.9%.
accepted.x: The PLFS figures cited for Andhra Pradesh in 2023–24 place open unemployment at 3.4% in rural areas and 5.9% in urban areas.
accepted.tq: Read the rural-urban comparison carefully; open unemployment differs from broader rural seasonal unemployment.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the defining test for identifying disguised unemployment?
o: Withdrawal of some workers leaves total output unchanged.
Workers remain unemployed throughout the business cycle.
Workers change jobs frequently in search of higher wages.
Withdrawal of some workers causes output to double.
accepted.x: Disguised unemployment is identified when removing some workers does not reduce total output, implying zero marginal productivity of those workers.
accepted.tq: Apply the marginal-productivity test to the employment situation.

accepted.s: In a family farm, eight persons work on land that requires only five persons, and removal of three workers does not reduce total output. This situation represents
o: Cyclical unemployment
Technological unemployment
Frictional unemployment
Disguised unemployment
accepted.x: The surplus workers appear employed but have zero marginal productivity because their withdrawal leaves total output unchanged.
accepted.tq: Use the output-after-withdrawal condition to identify hidden unemployment.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about disguised unemployment:
1. It is a form of hidden rather than open unemployment.
2. It is commonly observed among family members working on agricultural holdings.
3. Its marginal productivity of labour may be zero or negative.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Disguised unemployment is hidden unemployment, is common on family farms, and involves zero or negative marginal productivity for surplus workers.
accepted.tq: Check each defining feature before selecting the comprehensive option.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is a distinguishing feature of disguised unemployment in relation to PLFS headline unemployment rates?
o: It is fully captured because all workers report themselves as unemployed.
It is captured only during the contraction phase of the business cycle.
It is generally not captured because the persons appear to be employed.
It is measured exclusively through urban establishment surveys.
accepted.x: Persons in disguised unemployment appear employed, so this hidden form is not captured by headline unemployment rates in the same way as open unemployment.
accepted.tq: Distinguish apparent employment from measured open unemployment.

accepted.s: Cyclical unemployment arises primarily from
o: The seasonal closure of agricultural activities
A fall in aggregate demand for goods and services
The time taken to search for a new job
A mismatch between acquired skills and available jobs
accepted.x: Cyclical unemployment results from deficient aggregate demand during recession or depression, leading firms to reduce employment.
accepted.tq: Match the unemployment type with its immediate macroeconomic cause.
accepted.sec: Cyclical unemployment - cause and business-cycle phase  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Cyclical unemployment is most closely associated with which phase of the business cycle?
o: Contraction or trough
Stable equilibrium at potential output
Expansion or boom
Recovery after full employment
accepted.x: Cyclical unemployment is linked to the contraction or trough phase and begins to decline when recovery or boom starts.
accepted.tq: Link the cause of unemployment to the correct business-cycle phase.
accepted.sec: Cyclical unemployment - cause and business-cycle phase  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Assertion (A): Cyclical unemployment tends to decline when economic recovery begins.
Reason (R): Recovery is generally accompanied by an improvement in aggregate demand for goods and services.

Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
accepted.x: Both statements are true, and the rise in aggregate demand during recovery encourages firms to restore production and employment.
accepted.tq: Check whether the macroeconomic reason directly explains the movement in cyclical unemployment.
accepted.sec: Cyclical unemployment - cause and business-cycle phase  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to Keynes, unemployment in developed economies primarily results from
o: Excessive labour mobility
A surplus of agricultural workers
A mismatch caused only by technological change
Deficiency in effective demand
accepted.x: Keynes explained unemployment in developed economies mainly through deficiency in effective demand, which is associated with demand-deficient or cyclical unemployment.
accepted.tq: Associate the economist with the precise explanation rather than a related unemployment type.
accepted.sec: Cyclical unemployment - cause and business-cycle phase  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following best describes the basic nature of unemployment in India?
o: Entirely frictional and temporary
Predominantly technological and confined to manufacturing
Predominantly structural and long-run in character
Entirely cyclical and confined to recessions
accepted.x: Indian unemployment is basically structural because the demand for labour falls short of supply over the long run due to several structural factors.
accepted.tq: Separate the broad national character of unemployment from sector-specific forms.
accepted.sec: Nature of India's unemployment - predominant type and causes  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which combination best explains the structural nature of unemployment in India?
o: Only seasonal rainfall variations and tourism cycles
High labour mobility, labour-intensive production and low population growth
Rapid population growth, labour immobility and a shift towards capital-intensive production
Short job-search periods and temporary workplace transfers
accepted.x: Rapid population growth, labour immobility and the shift towards capital-intensive production contribute to a long-run shortfall of labour demand relative to supply.
accepted.tq: Select the option containing the structural causes rather than temporary causes.
accepted.sec: Nature of India's unemployment - predominant type and causes  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a structural cause of unemployment in India identified in the context of the secondary sector?
o: Jobless growth and inadequate focus on MSMEs
Rapid expansion of labour-intensive manufacturing generating abundant jobs
Slow infrastructure and delays in official paperwork
Neglected structural transformation of the secondary sector
accepted.x: Rapid expansion of labour-intensive manufacturing generating abundant jobs would reduce, rather than cause, structural unemployment. The other factors are identified structural impediments.
accepted.tq: Find the option that reverses the direction of a stated structural cause.
accepted.sec: Nature of India's unemployment - predominant type and causes  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding unemployment in India:
1. A large agricultural workforce contributes to seasonal and disguised unemployment.
2. Indian unemployment differs from the demand-deficient unemployment emphasised by Keynes for developed economies.
3. Underemployment is also a feature of the Indian labour market.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. India has substantial seasonal, disguised and underemployment, while its basic unemployment problem is structural rather than solely Keynesian demand deficiency.
accepted.tq: Combine the sectoral, theoretical and labour-market dimensions before choosing the code.
accepted.sec: Nature of India's unemployment - predominant type and causes  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following combinations reflects other causes associated with unemployment in India?
o: A complete shift towards labour-intensive manufacturing and export-led growth
Universal formal employment, high female labour force participation and perfect skill matching
Only temporary job search and absence of capital-intensive sectors
Skill-curriculum mismatch, a predominantly informal workforce and low female labour force participation
accepted.x: Skill-curriculum mismatch, approximately 90% informal employment and low female labour force participation are among the stated causes. Capital-intensive growth and limited export orientation also contribute to the problem.
accepted.tq: Choose the option that groups multiple related structural labour-market weaknesses.
accepted.sec: Nature of India's unemployment - predominant type and causes  [other exams]

accepted.s: Growth led mainly by capital-intensive IT and finance rather than labour-intensive manufacturing is associated with
o: The conversion of cyclical unemployment into frictional unemployment
A source of employment-generation limitations in India
The disappearance of underemployment in rural areas
A reduction in structural unemployment through mass job creation
accepted.x: Capital-intensive growth in sectors such as IT and finance does not generate employment on the scale of labour-intensive manufacturing, thereby contributing to employment limitations.
accepted.tq: Apply the labour-intensity distinction to the employment effect of growth.
accepted.sec: Nature of India's unemployment - predominant type and causes  [other exams]

accepted.s: Educated unemployment in India is predominantly associated with urban areas mainly because
o: Education automatically causes workers to leave the labour force.
Agricultural work is unavailable in every rural month.
Urban workers are excluded from all formal employment.
Educated persons are unable to find jobs matching their qualifications and industry requirements.
accepted.x: Educated unemployment is an urban phenomenon in which qualified persons fail to find employment matching their education and the needs of industry.
accepted.tq: Connect the location of educated unemployment with the qualification-job mismatch.

accepted.s: According to the India Skills Report 2024 figure cited, approximately what proportion of graduates was considered employable?
accepted.x: The cited India Skills Report 2024 estimate places the employability of graduates at approximately 46%.
accepted.tq: Retain the precise percentage instead of substituting a rounded majority figure.

accepted.s: According to PLFS 2025, the unemployment rate for persons with secondary schooling and above was
accepted.x: The cited PLFS 2025 figure for persons with secondary schooling and above was 6.5%, more than double the national rate.
accepted.tq: Use the exact education-linked unemployment figure and compare nearby alternatives.

accepted.s: For persons with secondary schooling and above, the PLFS 2025 unemployment rate was reported as
o: Higher in rural areas than in urban areas, at 7.2% and 5.9%, respectively
Equal in rural and urban areas, at 6.5% each
Higher in rural areas than in urban areas, at 7.2% and 6%, respectively
Higher in urban areas than in rural areas, at 7.2% and 6%, respectively
accepted.x: The cited PLFS 2025 rates were 7.2% in urban areas and 6% in rural areas for persons with secondary schooling and above.
accepted.tq: Compare both the direction and the values of the rural-urban figures.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the cited PLFS 2025 unemployment rates for youth aged 18–29 and for tertiary-educated youth, respectively?
accepted.x: The cited PLFS 2025 unemployment rate was 14.8% for youth aged 18–29 and rose to 29.4% for tertiary-educated youth.
accepted.tq: Keep the population groups separate when comparing closely related percentages.

accepted.s: What proportion of tertiary-educated youth was reported to be NEET in PLFS 2025?
accepted.x: The cited PLFS 2025 figure was 40.1% of tertiary-educated youth being NEET, meaning not in employment, education or training.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the NEET percentage from the unemployment percentages for the same broad group.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the cited unemployment rates among Gen Z graduates?
o: Male graduates 40.1% and female graduates 29.4%
Male graduates 11.9% and female graduates 14.8%
Male graduates 29% and female graduates 36.9%
Male graduates 36.9% and female graduates 29%
accepted.x: The cited figures for Gen Z graduates were 29% for males and 36.9% for females.
accepted.tq: Check the gender labels before comparing the two percentages.

accepted.s: The unemployment rate cited for Gen Z persons aged 15–26 was
accepted.x: The cited unemployment rate for Gen Z persons aged 15–26 was 11.9%.
accepted.tq: Match the age group with its own rate rather than using the youth aggregate figure.

accepted.s: A person working fewer than the normal number of hours is an example of
o: Invisible underemployment
Visible underemployment
Disguised unemployment only
Cyclical unemployment only
accepted.x: Visible underemployment involves working fewer than normal hours. It can be observed directly from the amount of work performed.
accepted.tq: Use the observable-hours distinction to separate visible from invisible underemployment.

accepted.s: An MBA graduate working full-time as a driver at a very low income is an example of
o: Seasonal unemployment
Frictional unemployment
Invisible underemployment
Visible underemployment
accepted.x: Invisible underemployment exists when a person works full-time but earns very little or works below their ability, as in the example of an MBA working as a driver.
accepted.tq: Look beyond the number of hours and identify underutilisation of skills or income.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes frictional unemployment from structural unemployment?
o: Frictional unemployment requires structural reform, whereas structural unemployment ends with a short job search.
Frictional unemployment exists only during depression, whereas structural unemployment disappears during recession.
Frictional unemployment is short-term job-search unemployment, whereas structural unemployment is long-term skill-job mismatch.
Frictional unemployment is caused by technology, whereas structural unemployment is caused by seasonal agriculture.
accepted.x: Frictional unemployment results from the temporary time lag involved in changing or searching for jobs, while structural unemployment is long-term and arises from a mismatch between skills and available jobs.
accepted.tq: Separate the two types using cause and duration together.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Frictional unemployment can exist even when the economy is at full employment.
2. Structural unemployment is deep-rooted and may require reskilling or structural reform.
3. Frictional unemployment is generally permanent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because frictional unemployment is normally short-term and temporary.
accepted.tq: Use the duration and policy-response contrast to reject the reversed statement.

accepted.s: A worker voluntarily leaves a job and spends a short period searching for a better one. This is an example of
o: Frictional unemployment
Disguised unemployment
Cyclical unemployment
Structural unemployment
accepted.x: The temporary gap caused by quitting one job and searching for another is frictional or search unemployment.
accepted.tq: Identify the unemployment type from the worker's transition between jobs.

accepted.s: Which situation best illustrates structural unemployment?
o: A firm laying off workers during a recession
A worker changing jobs after voluntarily quitting
A farm worker remaining idle during the agricultural off-season
A labour-intensive economy shifting towards capital-intensive production
accepted.x: A shift from labour-intensive to capital-intensive production changes the demand for labour and creates a long-term structural mismatch.
accepted.tq: Match the example to long-term structural change rather than a temporary interruption.

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
o: Structural unemployment — temporary job-search gap
Frictional unemployment — needs immediate structural reform
Frictional unemployment — normal even at full employment
Structural unemployment — exists only during economic boom
accepted.x: Frictional unemployment is a normal feature that can exist even at full employment. Structural unemployment is long-run and deep-rooted, not a temporary search gap or a boom-only phenomenon.
accepted.tq: Find the correctly matched pair after rejecting reversed definitions and durations.
